q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of curd or dahi per kg?
title: Curd carbon footprint per kg
short: Take the milk per kg of curd from your plant's yield and multiply by the milk figure from your procurement. Add boiler fuel for pasteurising, incubation and chilling electricity, and the cups or pouches, then divide plant energy by kg packed.

ul: Milk per kg of curd, from fat and SNF standardisation records.
Culture and any skim milk powder added.
Pasteurising and homogenising with boiler steam.
Incubation rooms and cold rooms on electricity.
Cleaning in place and effluent treatment.

p: Milk is usually most of the total. Report per kg packed, and per cup or pouch with its net weight.

example.title: Worked example: curd section per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 40,700 / 200,000 = 0.203 kg CO2 per kg
Add milk and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
